title: Small RNA Sequencing (Mouse Blood)
author: Dain Lee
license_note: figshare article detail endpoint license.name: CC BY 4.0

steps.title: Polyadenylate input RNA
steps.instruction: Polyadenylate the input RNA to create a priming sequence for the oligo(dT) primer, as required by the SMARTer smRNA‑Seq Kit for Illumina.

steps.title: First‑strand cDNA synthesis
steps.instruction: Prime first‑strand cDNA synthesis with the 3’ smRNA dT Primer using PrimeScript™ Reverse Transcriptase (RT, cat no 2680, Takara Bio, Otsu, Japan).

steps.title: Template‑switch and add second adapter
steps.instruction: When PrimeScript RT reaches the 5’ end of each RNA template, it adds nontemplated nucleotides that anneal to the SMART smRNA Oligo (enhanced with locked nucleic acid technology); the enzyme then uses this oligo as a template to append a second adapter sequence to the 3’ end of the first‑strand cDNA.

steps.title: PCR amplify with Illumina adapters
steps.instruction: Amplify the cDNA by PCR using a Forward PCR Primer that binds the sequence added by the SMART smRNA Oligo and a Reverse PCR Primer that binds the sequence added by the 3’ smRNA dT Primer, thereby incorporating full‑length Illumina adapters (including index sequences) required for clustering.

steps.title: Validate library quality
steps.instruction: Assess each library’s size, purity, and concentration on an Agilent Bioanalyzer.

steps.title: Pool libraries and sequence
steps.instruction: Pool the validated libraries in equimolar amounts and sequence them on an Illumina NovaSeq instrument.

steps.title: Process sequencing data
steps.instruction: Perform image decomposition and calculate quality values using Illumina pipeline modules provided by Macrogen, Inc. (Daejeon, South Korea).
